spec.name: Earnings drift v6
spec.notes: Rank names by the latest earnings surprise and hold through the drift.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.9, annual return 5%, maximum drawdown 4%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.90 to 1.93 (change +0.03).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.90 to 1.90. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.87 (as submitted, 8 bps: 1.90); it breaks even at 132.5 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.90 against 1.90 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 1.20 against 1.90 in research, a gap of +0.70.
The best year gives 26% of total P&L (year 6) and calm regimes give 88%; Sharpe is 2.12 in calm and 1.11 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.02, so the claimed 1.90 becomes 1.88 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.92 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 0.51).
The signal has no numeric windows or parameters to perturb.
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 30% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 21% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
